# 06 - Semi-Solid, Quasi-Solid, and Gel-Electrolyte Batteries

Acquisition method: Web research note synthesized from public sources.

Primary sources:

- IEA, Global EV Outlook 2025, Electric vehicle batteries: https://www.iea.org/reports/global-ev-outlook-2025/electric-vehicle-batteries
- Stellantis and Factorial, 2026 demonstration fleet: https://www.stellantis.com/en/news/press-releases/2024/october/stellantis-and-factorial-take-next-step-to-accelerate-the-future-of-electric-vehicles-with-solid-state-battery-technology
- Stellantis and Factorial, 2025 cell validation: https://www.stellantis.com/en/news/press-releases/2025/april/stellantis-and-factorial-energy-reach-key-milestone-in-solid-state-battery-development
- 24M SemiSolid electrode technology: https://24-m.com/liforever

## What It Is

Semi-solid and quasi-solid batteries reduce or immobilize the liquid electrolyte rather than eliminating it completely. Designs may use gel-like electrolyte, hybrid solid-liquid electrolyte, thick slurry electrodes, or other approaches that sit between conventional lithium-ion and all-solid-state cells.

## Automotive Relevance Today

This category is highly relevant because many early products marketed as "solid-state" are likely to be semi-solid or quasi-solid first. IEA explicitly warns that solid-state is often used broadly and that first commercial products may use gel-like electrolyte or small volumes of liquid electrolyte.

Factorial's FEST technology, used in Stellantis programs, is often described in industry coverage as quasi-solid or semi-solid because it uses a lithium-metal anode and proprietary electrolyte system rather than a conventional liquid-only lithium-ion design.

## Strengths

Semi-solid designs try to capture some benefits of solid-state while reducing scale-up risk:

- Higher energy density than conventional lithium-ion.
- Improved safety from less flammable electrolyte.
- Easier manufacturing transition than all-solid-state.
- Potential compatibility with existing lithium-ion processes.

Stellantis and Factorial report automotive-sized 77 Ah cells with 375 Wh/kg, 15%-90% charging in 18 minutes at room temperature, operation from -30 C to 45 C, and over 600 cycles progressing toward automotive qualification.

24M's SemiSolid approach emphasizes simplified construction, binderless electrodes, cost reduction, abuse tolerance, and recycling benefits.

## Weaknesses

The category is hard to evaluate because terminology is inconsistent. A semi-solid cell may still have liquid electrolyte-related risks and may not deliver the full safety or energy-density promise of all-solid-state batteries.

Cost is also unresolved. Limited-volume semi-solid packs can be extremely expensive, and early high-energy products may be symbolic or premium-only.

## Future Development

Semi-solid systems may become a transition technology:

- Demonstration fleets in 2026.
- Premium limited-volume vehicles first.
- Gradual improvement in manufacturing yield and pack integration.
- Potential use in long-range or performance trims before mass-market adoption.

## Commercialization Outlook

More credible in the near term than all-solid-state at mass scale. The likely path is limited production, demonstration fleets, and premium applications before broad deployment.

## Implications for Older EV Value

If semi-solid vehicles offer materially longer range at similar pack weight, they could affect perception of older EVs. But if early costs are high and volumes low, near-term depreciation impact on mainstream used EVs should be limited.
